parsed.summary: Lean states the paper's sharp Ehrhart volume inequality: a compact convex set in ℝⁿ (n>0) with nonempty interior, barycenter 0 and interior lattice points exactly {0} has Lebesgue volume at most (n+1)ⁿ/n!. It also states that the simplex (n+1)Δₙ−(1,…,1) has barycenter 0 and volume (n+1)ⁿ/n!, and that a body attaining the bound exists. The statements match the paper. The only caveats are cosmetic: 'normalizedVolume' is plain Lebesgue volume, and the Lean version requires n>0.

glossary.plain: ℝⁿ as Fin n → ℝ with the product Lebesgue measure
Lebesgue measure of K as a real number (toReal)
glossary.note: The name suggests a normalization, but it is the plain volume. toReal is harmless for compact K, whose volume is finite.
Junk values occur only if vol K = 0 or K is not integrable. The theorems assume nonempty interior and compactness, so this is avoided.

glossary.plain: Compact convex K with nonempty interior, barycenter 0, and int(K) ∩ ℤⁿ = {0}

lean_claims.plain: For every n, the barycenter of (n+1)Δₙ−(1,…,1) is 0.
For n>0 there is a compact convex body K with nonempty interior, barycenter 0, int(K) ∩ ℤⁿ = {0}, and vol(K) = (n+1)ⁿ/n!.
For n>0 and S ⊂ ℝⁿ convex, compact, with nonempty interior, barycenter 0 and int(S) ∩ ℤⁿ = {0}, vol(S) ≤ (n+1)ⁿ/n!.

paper_claims.plain: A full-dimensional compact convex K ⊂ ℝⁿ with barycenter 0 and int(K) ∩ ℤⁿ = {0} has vol(K) ≤ (n+1)ⁿ/n!.
The simplex (n+1)Δₙ − (1,…,1) has barycenter 0, no other interior lattice point, and volume (n+1)ⁿ/n!.

coverage.why: The hypotheses and conclusion are the same. Lean adds n>0, which is the intended range.

Lean packages the existence of an extremizer. It is witnessed by the simplex, with the barycenter and volume facts given by the two simplex theorems. The simplex theorems do not themselves state that the simplex has no other interior lattice point; that is carried only inside the existence statement.
